[[File:BVDBeek(AMJ).jpg|thumb|Dr. Bram van de Beek]]
'''Abraham "Bram" van de Beek''' (born 9 October 1946) is a Dutch Reformed theologian. He was a professor of biblical and systematic theology at [[Leiden University]] between 1981 and 2000. Subsequently he was professor of [[Christian symbolism]] at the [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]] until 2010.

==Career==
Van de Beek was born on 9 October 1946 in [[Lunteren]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.godgeleerdheid.vu.nl/nl/Images/Beek-van-de-Bram-CV_tcm238-75910.pdf |title=Curriculum vitae Abraham van de Beek |language=Dutch |publisher=VU University Amsterdam |date= |accessdate=19 March 2016 |archive-date=10 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510011130/http://www.godgeleerdheid.vu.nl/nl/Images/Beek-van-de-Bram-CV_tcm238-75910.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.protestant.nu/Encyclopedie/tabid/359/Page/Beek,%20Abraham%20van%20de/Default.aspx Beek, Bram van de] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130033806/http://www.protestant.nu/Encyclopedie/tabid/359/Page/Beek,%20Abraham%20van%20de/Default.aspx |date=2018-01-30 }} at protestant.nu</ref> Between 1964 and 1970 he studied theology at [[Utrecht University]], obtaining a master's degree under [[A. A. van Ruler|Arnold van Ruler]]. Four years later, although not have studied biology, he earned a PhD in botany with a thesis on brambles titled ''Die Brombeeren des Geldrische distriktes innerhalb der Flora der Niederlande'' under F.P. Jonker at the same university. Van de Beek then moved to [[Leiden University]] and earned a DTh in 1980 with a thesis titled ''De menselijke persoon van Christus'' under supervision of [[Hendrikus Berkhof]].<ref name=cv/><ref name=theologie>{{cite web|url=https://www.theologie.nl/oeuvreprijs-voor-bram-van-de-beek/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231027151734/https://www.theologie.nl/oeuvreprijs-voor-bram-van-de-beek/ |title=Oeuvreprijs voor Bram van de Beek |language=Dutch |publisher=theologie.nl |date=11 November 2022 |archive-date=27 October 2023}}</ref> Although having written a thesis in botany Van de Beek never considered a career in the field, but kept interested and continued publishing in it. In 2021 he published an article on brambles in South Africa.<ref name=theologie/>

Van de Beek was a minister in the [[Dutch Reformed Church]] between 1970 and 1981.<ref name=cv/> At [[Lexmond]], his first parish, he dealt with twenty vehicular deaths in four years.<ref name=theologie/> In 1974 he moved parish to [[Vriezenveen]] and in 1979 to [[Raamsdonk]].<ref name=theologie/> In 1981 he started as professor of biblical and systematic theology at Leiden University.<ref name=cv/> At that point in time he had only one publication in the field.<ref name=theologie/> He remained a professor at Leiden University until 2000, in that year he became professor of [[Christian symbolism]] at the [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]].<ref name=cv/> From 2005 to 2008 he was dean of the faculty of theology. In 2010 he took up an early retirement due to an illness of his wife.<ref name=theologie/> Van de Beek also served as professor not paid from university funds at [[Stellenbosch University]] from 2003.

==Honours and awards==
In 1997 Van de Beek was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/3844 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160319161037/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/3844 |title=Bram van de Beek |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=19 March 2016 |accessdate=19 March 2016}}</ref> In 2012, a ''[[Festschrift]]'' was published in his honour: ''Strangers and Pilgrims on Earth: Essays in Honour of Abraham van de Beek''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Strangers and Pilgrims on Earth |url=https://brill.com/edcollbook/title/20922?language=en |publisher=[[Brill Publishers]] |access-date=13 January 2024}}</ref> In November 2022, during the night of theology, Van de Beek received an award for his [[complete works]], which comprised over 6000 pages excluding publications in English.<ref name=theologie/>
